videos.name: Y Combinator
videos.title: Building AI for the $650B Home Services Market
videos.description:
Broccoli (YC W22) is building an AI front office for home services businesses, answering calls, following up with leads, and booking appointments across voice and text.

Today, they serve more than 500 customers, are booking jobs at a run rate of over $1 billion a year, and expect to end the year at more than $60 million in ARR, up from zero just two years ago, after recently raising a $30 million Series B.

In this Founder Fireside, Broccoli’s founders AJ Jain and Aditya Ketkar join YC's Gustaf Alstromer to share the long path to finding that business, from an earlier EV startup that never found product-market fit to visiting 140 contractors across the Bay Area to understand their biggest problems firsthand. They explain how embedding inside a plumbing company led to the first version of Broccoli, why answering missed calls became the wedge, and how AI could eventually reshape the work of technicians themselves.

https://www.broccoli.com

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: Why Agents Love Supabase — with Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson
videos.description:
Why do AI agents keep choosing Supabase—and what changes when the agent becomes the user?

Supabase co-founders Paul Copplestone (CEO) and Ant Wilson (CTO) join swyx for their first podcast together after a $0 to $10B speedrun as the preeminent open source, fully remote Postgres platform company. We have watched them grow from a humble Firebase alternative launched during Covid, to now being a full preferred backend for AI-built applications: long-running compute beside the database, declarative schemas, Postgres storage and reliability, Turso, developer memes, community-led distribution, and product-led sales.

The episode opens with swyx’s commentary on Supabase Select and the company’s journey from zero to a $10B valuation in six years as an open-source, fully remote company. swyx also discusses his seed investment in Supabase and its sponsorship of Latent Space.

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: How Anthropic ships the #1 LLM in the World — with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang
videos.description:
An agent’s sandbox can die without taking the whole agent with it. That’s the idea behind “the brain and the hands,” Anthropic’s architecture for Claude Managed Agents.

Now that the dust has settled on Opus 5.5, it is universally agreed to be the best model in the world. In this conversation with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang, Anthropic’s Heads of Engineering and of Product, goes inside the systems that turn model capabilities into products developers can use.

We cover:

- Why Anthropic separated the agent harness, session state and execution environment.
- Letting agents use credentials without putting those credentials inside their sandboxes.
- Rebuilding the Messages API from Python to Rust with Claude—and verifying the rewrite with shadow traffic.
- Preventing model distillation while preserving the developer experience.
- Memory, “dreaming,” agent evaluations and the work still left for human engineers.
- How Anthropic’s own teams use Claude while keeping responsibility for their code and writing.

The episode opens with swyx’s look at Anthropic’s S-1: revenue per employee, compute efficiency, and the improvement and investment loops behind the business.

**Related links**

- [Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5) — Performance, pricing and safeguards.
- [The brain and the hands](https://www.anthropic.com/research/managed-agents) — The Managed Agents architecture.
- [How Anthropic contains Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-we-contain-claude) — Isolation, credentials and network controls.
- [Harnesses for long-running agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents) — Maintaining progress across context windows.
